Chart types

Source: vignettes/chart-types.Rmd
chart-types.Rmd

Measurements and ranges

Each row is one day. Its position supplies x, name labels the day and y is the mean temperature in °C. A range column extends from the day’s low to its high. With these names, hchart(temperatures, "columnrange") reads the columns directly. Use hcaes(low = minimum, high = maximum) if your columns have different names.

Show temperature data 
# fmt: skip
temperatures <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name, ~y, ~low, ~high,
  "Mon", 15,   12,    18,
  "Tue", 17,   13,    21,
  "Wed", 14,   11,    17,
  "Thu", 16,   12,    20,
  "Fri", 18,   14,    22
)
Show all temperature charts in R 
gallery(
  c(
    "line",
    "spline",
    "area",
    "streamgraph",
    "areaspline",
    "arearange",
    "areasplinerange",
    "columnrange",
    "errorbar",
    "dumbbell",
    "polar line",
    "polar columnrange"
  ),
  function(label) {
    type <- sub("^polar ", "", label)
    hchart(
      temperatures,
      type,
      name = "Temperature",
      colorByPoint = TRUE,
      lineColor = "#2980b9",
      fillColor = "#2980b966",
      tooltip = list(valueSuffix = " °C")
    ) |>
      hc_chart(
        type = type,
        polar = startsWith(label, "polar")
      ) |>
      hc_xAxis(categories = temperatures$name) |>
      hc_yAxis(title = list(text = ""), visible = type != "streamgraph")
  }
)

Quantities by category

Each visit appears once, at the last shopping step it reached (name). Bars, columns, cylinders and slices show how the 100 visits ended (y). Bars and columns start at zero; polar columns arrange the same quantities around a circle. A funnel counts everyone who reached each step: 100 viewed products, 66 added to cart, 42 started checkout and 24 purchased. For variable-width columns and variable-radius slices, z is the illustrative average session duration in minutes, available for all four steps. Variwide uses it for column width; variable pie uses it for radius, with zero as the lower bound. The treemap and packed bubbles split each stage by acquisition source. The word cloud compares stage and source totals.

Show shopping data 
# fmt: skip
shopping <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,         ~y, ~z,
  "Viewed",      34,  2.5,
  "Added",       24,    6,
  "Checkout",    18,    9,
  "Purchased",   24,    8
)

# fmt: skip
shopping_sources <- tibble::tribble(
  ~stage,      ~source, ~value,
  "Viewed",   "Search",     18,
  "Viewed",   "Social",     10,
  "Viewed",   "Direct",      6,
  "Added",    "Search",     13,
  "Added",    "Social",      7,
  "Added",    "Direct",      4,
  "Checkout", "Search",      9,
  "Checkout", "Social",      6,
  "Checkout", "Direct",      3,
  "Purchased","Search",    12,
  "Purchased","Social",     8,
  "Purchased","Direct",     4
)
Show all shopping charts in R 
gallery(
  c(
    "bar",
    "column",
    "cylinder",
    "columnpyramid",
    "variwide",
    "polar column",
    "pie",
    "variablepie",
    "lollipop",
    "dotplot",
    "item",
    "waterfall",
    "packedbubble",
    "treemap",
    "wordcloud",
    "funnel",
    "pyramid",
    "funnel3d",
    "pyramid3d"
  ),
  function(label) {
    type <- sub("^polar ", "", label)
    points <- shopping
    if (type %in% c("funnel", "pyramid", "funnel3d", "pyramid3d")) {
      points$y <- rev(cumsum(rev(points$y)))
    }
    if (type == "packedbubble") {
      return(hchart(
        shopping_sources,
        type,
        hcaes(group = stage, name = source, value = value),
        minSize = "16%",
        maxSize = "49%",
        zMin = 0,
        layoutAlgorithm = list(splitSeries = TRUE, seriesInteraction = FALSE),
        dataLabels = list(
          enabled = TRUE,
          format = "{point.name}",
          style = list(fontSize = "9px")
        ),
        tooltip = list(
          pointFormat = "{series.name} / {point.name}: {point.value} visits"
        )
      ))
    }
    if (type == "treemap") {
      nodes <- bind_rows(
        transmute(shopping, id = name, name),
        transmute(
          shopping_sources,
          id = paste(stage, source, sep = "-"),
          parent = stage,
          name = source,
          value
        )
      )
      return(hchart(
        nodes,
        type,
        levels = list(
          list(
            level = 1,
            colorByPoint = TRUE,
            dataLabels = list(
              enabled = TRUE,
              align = "left",
              verticalAlign = "top",
              format = "{point.name}",
              style = list(fontSize = "10px", fontWeight = "normal")
            )
          ),
          list(level = 2, colorVariation = list(key = "brightness", to = 0.35))
        ),
        dataLabels = list(enabled = FALSE),
        tooltip = list(
          pointFormat = "{point.parent} / {point.name}: {point.value} visits"
        )
      ))
    }
    if (type == "wordcloud") {
      words <- bind_rows(
        transmute(shopping, name, weight = y),
        summarise(
          group_by(shopping_sources, name = source),
          weight = sum(value)
        )
      )
      return(hchart(
        words,
        type,
        name = "Visits",
        rotation = list(from = 0, to = 0)
      ))
    }
    hchart(points, type, name = "Visits", colorByPoint = TRUE) |>
      hc_plotOptions(
        pie = list(dataLabels = list(distance = 8)),
        variablepie = list(
          zMin = 0,
          dataLabels = list(distance = 8),
          tooltip = list(
            pointFormat = "{point.name}: {point.y} visits<br>Average session: {point.z} min"
          )
        ),
        variwide = list(
          tooltip = list(
            pointFormat = "{point.name}: {point.y} visits<br>Average session: {point.z} min"
          )
        )
      ) |>
      hc_xAxis(
        categories = points$name,
        labels = if (startsWith(label, "polar")) {
          list(distance = 5, style = list(fontSize = "10px"))
        }
      ) |>
      hc_chart(
        type = type,
        polar = startsWith(label, "polar"),
        options3d = list(
          enabled = type %in% c("cylinder", "funnel3d", "pyramid3d"),
          alpha = 12,
          beta = 15
        )
      )
  }
)

Relationships and hierarchies

Each row connects a parent team (from) to a subteam (to). The link’s weight is the subteam’s headcount. Tree and sunburst charts express the same hierarchy with id and parent. Network nodes use marker.radius to show team size.

Show team data 
# fmt: skip
teams <- tibble::tribble(
  ~from,     ~to,       ~weight,
  "Studio",  "Design",       12,
  "Studio",  "Build",        18,
  "Design",  "Web",           7,
  "Design",  "Print",         5,
  "Build",   "Apps",         10,
  "Build",   "Data",          5,
  "Build",   "Tools",         3
)

team_sizes <- bind_rows(
  teams |>
    group_by(from) |>
    summarise(headcount = sum(weight), .groups = "drop") |>
    rename(id = from),
  transmute(teams, id = to, headcount = weight)
) |>
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    marker = lapply(
      4 + 10 * sqrt(headcount / max(headcount)),
      function(radius) list(radius = radius)
    )
  )
Show all team charts in R 
gallery(
  c(
    "sankey",
    "dependencywheel",
    "arcdiagram",
    "networkgraph",
    "organization",
    "treegraph",
    "sunburst"
  ),
  function(type) {
    if (type == "networkgraph") {
      return(hchart(
        teams,
        type,
        nodes = list_parse(team_sizes),
        layoutAlgorithm = list(enableSimulation = FALSE),
        dataLabels = list(
          enabled = TRUE,
          linkFormat = "",
          style = list(
            fontSize = "9px",
            textOutline = "none",
            fontWeight = "normal"
          )
        ),
        tooltip = list(nodeFormat = "{point.name}: {point.headcount} people")
      ))
    }
    if (type == "organization") {
      return(hchart(
        teams,
        type,
        color = "#47475c",
        colorByPoint = FALSE,
        nodeWidth = 54,
        nodePadding = 8,
        dataLabels = list(
          nodeFormat = "{point.name}",
          style = list(
            color = "#ffffff",
            fontSize = "10px",
            fontWeight = "normal",
            textOutline = "none"
          )
        )
      ))
    }
    if (type %in% c("treegraph", "sunburst")) {
      nodes <- bind_rows(
        tibble(id = "Studio", name = "Studio"),
        transmute(teams, id = to, parent = from, name = to, value = weight)
      )
      if (type == "sunburst") {
        return(hchart(
          nodes,
          type,
          levels = list(list(level = 2, colorByPoint = TRUE))
        ))
      }
      return(hchart(nodes, type))
    }
    hchart(teams, type)
  }
)

For a network with an igraph layout, see the igraph example.

Positions, bubbles and wind

Each point is a South American capital or seat of government at its longitude (x) and latitude (y). The rounded coordinates come from Natural Earth’s populated places. Illustrative wind speed in m/s supplies bubble size and the third dimension (z), vector length and wind-barb value. direction gives the angle in degrees. Hover over a point to see the city and wind speed. The 3D scatter also labels the cities. A hollow circle in a wind-barb series means calm wind (below 0.3 m/s). All the illustrative speeds here are at least 3 m/s.

Show capital data and illustrative winds 
# fmt: skip
capitals <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,             ~x,     ~y, ~speed, ~direction,
  "Bogotá",      -74.09,   4.60,      6,         70,
  "Caracas",     -66.92,  10.50,      7,        100,
  "Georgetown",  -58.17,   6.80,      4,         80,
  "Paramaribo",  -55.17,   5.84,      5,         65,
  "Quito",       -78.50,  -0.21,      4,        160,
  "Lima",        -77.05, -12.05,      8,        180,
  "La Paz",      -68.15, -16.50,      6,        225,
  "Sucre",       -65.26, -19.04,      5,        250,
  "Brasília",    -47.92, -15.78,      3,         90,
  "Asunción",    -57.63, -25.29,      7,        120,
  "Santiago",    -70.65, -33.44,      5,        210,
  "Montevideo",  -56.19, -34.91,      9,        150,
  "Buenos Aires",-58.43, -34.61,     11,        135
) |> mutate(z = speed)
Show all capital charts in R 
gallery(
  c("scatter", "bubble", "scatter3d", "vector", "windbarb", "polygon"),
  function(type) {
    points <- arrange(capitals, x)
    if (type == "polygon") {
      points <- points[chull(points$x, points$y), ]
    }
    if (type == "windbarb") {
      hc <- hchart(
        points,
        "scatter",
        id = "cities",
        color = "#47475c",
        marker = list(enabled = FALSE),
        dataLabels = list(enabled = FALSE),
        enableMouseTracking = FALSE,
        showInLegend = FALSE
      ) |>
        hc_add_series(
          points,
          "windbarb",
          hcaes(value = speed),
          color = "#47475c",
          dataGrouping = list(enabled = FALSE),
          onSeries = "cities",
          yOffset = 0,
          name = "Wind"
        )
    } else if (type == "vector") {
      hc <- hchart(
        points,
        type,
        hcaes(length = speed),
        color = "#47475c",
        vectorLength = 24,
        lineWidth = 2,
        name = "Wind"
      )
    } else {
      hc <- hchart(points, type, name = "Capitals", color = "#47475c")
    }
    hc |>
      hc_chart(
        type = if (type == "windbarb") "scatter" else type,
        options3d = list(
          enabled = type == "scatter3d",
          alpha = 20,
          beta = 32,
          depth = 160
        )
      ) |>
      hc_plotOptions(
        series = list(
          dataLabels = list(
            enabled = type == "scatter3d",
            format = "{point.name}",
            style = list(fontSize = "9px", fontWeight = "normal")
          )
        ),
        bubble = list(zMin = 0, minSize = 5, maxSize = "18%")
      ) |>
      hc_tooltip(
        headerFormat = "",
        pointFormat = "{point.name}: {point.speed} m/s"
      ) |>
      hc_xAxis(min = -82, max = -43, title = list(text = "Longitude")) |>
      hc_yAxis(min = -40, max = 15, title = list(text = "Latitude"))
  }
)

Gridded measurements

Each cell has a column (x), a row (y) and a measurement (value). A heatmap colors rectangular cells, a tilemap uses hexagons, and a contour joins locations with the same value.

Show R code 
volcano_colors <- c("#000004", "#56106E", "#BB3754", "#F98C0A", "#FCFFA4")
cells <- expand.grid(x = 0:5, y = 0:5) |> mutate(value = sin(x) + cos(y))
Show R code 
gallery(c("heatmap", "tilemap", "contour"), function(type) {
  hchart(cells, type) |>
    hc_colorAxis(
      min = -2,
      max = 2,
      stops = color_stops(colors = volcano_colors)
    )
})

Other examples

Intervals use start and end positions. A Venn diagram sizes intersections by sets and value, and a solid gauge displays a single measurement (y).

Timeline

Five milestones in Albert Einstein’s life. Spacing follows calendar years. ETH Library biography.

Show R code 
event_colors <- unlist(hc_theme("smpl")$colors)[c(2, 3, 1, 4, 5)]
events <- tibble::tibble(
  color = event_colors,
  x = c(1879, 1905, 1921, 1933, 1955),
  name = c(
    "Born in Ulm",
    "Special relativity",
    "Physics Nobel",
    "Princeton",
    "Dies in Princeton"
  ),
  # Deeper shades of the five marker colors keep the white lettering legible.
  dataLabels = lapply(
    c("#246E9E", "#17774B", "#B34605", "#846707", "#354D63"),
    function(fill) list(backgroundColor = fill)
  )
)
hchart(
  events,
  "timeline",
  hcaes(color = color),
  name = "Albert Einstein",
  colorByPoint = TRUE,
  dataLabels = list(
    format = "{point.x} · {point.name}",
    color = "#FFFFFF",
    borderWidth = 0,
    style = list(
      fontSize = "11px",
      fontWeight = "normal",
      textOutline = "none"
    )
  )
) |>
  hc_xAxis(type = "linear", visible = FALSE) |>
  hc_yAxis(visible = FALSE, title = list(text = NULL)) |>
  hc_tooltip(headerFormat = "", pointFormat = "{point.x} · {point.name}") |>
  hc_size(height = 300)

Task intervals

Each row spans two dates. Map the start to x, the end to x2 and the lane’s zero-based index to y. Here, twelve tasks share four team lanes. The three phases use different series and colors. grouping = FALSE places each series on the same team lane, while the start and finish dates determine its horizontal position.

Show R code 
# fmt: skip
tasks <- tibble::tribble(
  ~team,      ~phase,    ~task,        ~offset, ~days, ~progress,
  "Data",     "Prepare","Extract",         0,     3,         1,
  "Data",     "Build",  "Clean",           3,     4,         1,
  "Data",     "Review", "Validate",        7,     3,       0.8,
  "Research", "Prepare","Scope",           0,     4,         1,
  "Research", "Build",  "Analyse",         4,     5,       0.8,
  "Research", "Review", "Review",          9,     3,       0.3,
  "Design",   "Prepare","Wireframes",      1,     3,         1,
  "Design",   "Build",  "Prototype",       4,     4,       0.9,
  "Design",   "Review", "Test",            8,     4,       0.2,
  "Platform", "Prepare","Configure",       0,     2,         1,
  "Platform", "Build",  "Integrate",       5,     5,       0.5,
  "Platform", "Review", "Deploy",         11,     2,         0
) |>
  mutate(
    phase = factor(phase, levels = c("Prepare", "Build", "Review")),
    start = base::as.Date("2025-01-06") + offset,
    finish = start + days,
    lane = match(team, unique(team)) - 1L
  )
hchart(
  tasks,
  "xrange",
  hcaes(
    x = start,
    x2 = finish,
    y = lane,
    group = phase,
    name = task,
    partialFill = progress
  ),
  colorByPoint = FALSE,
  dataLabels = list(
    enabled = TRUE,
    format = "{point.name}",
    style = list(
      fontSize = "10px",
      color = "contrast",
      fontWeight = "normal",
      textOutline = "1px contrast"
    )
  )
) |>
  hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "")) |>
  hc_yAxis(
    categories = unique(tasks$team),
    reversed = TRUE,
    title = list(text = "")
  ) |>
  hc_colors(event_colors[1:3]) |>
  hc_plotOptions(xrange = list(grouping = FALSE, pointWidth = 22)) |>
  hc_tooltip(
    pointFormat = "{point.name}<br>{point.x:%e %b} to {point.x2:%e %b}"
  ) |>
  hc_size(height = 330)

The same twelve intervals can be shown as Gantt tasks. Assign an ID to each task and link the tasks within each team with dependency.

Show R code 
schedule <- tasks |>
  group_by(team) |>
  mutate(id = paste(team, row_number(), sep = "-"), dependency = lag(id)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(
    color = event_colors[as.integer(phase)],
    name = paste(team, task, sep = ": "),
    id,
    start = datetime_to_timestamp(start),
    end = datetime_to_timestamp(finish),
    completed = progress,
    dependency
  )
hchart(schedule, "gantt", hcaes(color = color), name = "Tasks") |>
  hc_yAxis(
    labels = list(
      levels = list(list(level = 1, style = list(fontWeight = "normal")))
    )
  ) |>
  hc_plotOptions(
    gantt = list(
      dataLabels = list(
        style = list(
          fontWeight = "normal",
          color = "#FFFFFF",
          textOutline = "none"
        )
      )
    )
  ) |>
  hc_size(height = 500)

See the release schedule with dependencies and completion bars.

Venn intersections

These illustrative counts describe overlapping skills among 100 analysts. Pairwise intersections include the ten analysts who use all three tools.

Show R code 
skills <- tibble::tibble(
  sets = list(
    list("R"),
    list("Python"),
    list("SQL"),
    list("R", "Python"),
    list("R", "SQL"),
    list("Python", "SQL"),
    list("R", "Python", "SQL")
  ),
  name = c(
    "R",
    "Python",
    "SQL",
    "R and Python",
    "R and SQL",
    "Python and SQL",
    "All three"
  ),
  value = c(57, 48, 45, 20, 22, 18, 10)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(label = ifelse(lengths(sets) == 1L, name, as.character(value)))

hchart(
  skills,
  "venn",
  name = "Analysts",
  opacity = 1,
  borderColor = "#ffffff",
  borderWidth = 2,
  dataLabels = list(
    format = "{point.label}",
    style = list(
      fontSize = "11px",
      color = "#ffffff",
      fontWeight = "normal",
      textOutline = "2px #253238"
    )
  )
) |>
  hc_colors(c("#216595", "#367444", "#936816")) |>
  hc_tooltip(pointFormat = "{point.name}: {point.value} analysts") |>
  hc_caption(
    text = "Illustrative skills of 100 analysts; intersection counts include all three tools.",
    style = list(fontSize = "11px")
  ) |>
  hc_size(height = 310)

solidgauge

Show R code 
col_stops <- data.frame(
  q = c(0.15, 0.4, .8),
  c = c('#55BF3B', '#DDDF0D', '#DF5353'),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

highchart() |>
  hc_chart(type = "solidgauge") |>
  hc_pane(
    startAngle = -90,
    endAngle = 90,
    background = list(
      outerRadius = '100%',
      innerRadius = '60%',
      shape = "arc"
    )
  ) |>
  hc_tooltip(enabled = FALSE) |>
  hc_yAxis(
    stops = list_parse2(col_stops),
    lineWidth = 0,
    minorTickWidth = 0,
    tickAmount = 2,
    min = 0,
    max = 100,
    labels = list(y = 26, style = list(fontSize = "22px"))
  ) |>
  hc_add_series(
    data = 90,
    dataLabels = list(
      y = -50,
      borderWidth = 0,
      useHTML = TRUE,
      style = list(fontSize = "40px")
    )
  ) |>
  hc_size(height = 300)

Related articles

Explore the finished world tile map, word cloud and wind map in Showcase.

See Icons and pictograms for image markers, icons in tooltips and symbols that represent individual items.

The Maps and Stock articles cover geographic and financial series. The bundle gallery has an example for every registered series type.

Show the gallery layout code 
gallery <- function(types, draw) {
  charts <- lapply(types, function(type) {
    draw(type) |>
      hc_title(text = type, style = list(fontSize = "16px")) |>
      hc_legend(enabled = FALSE) |>
      hc_tooltip(outside = TRUE) |>
      hc_size(height = 235)
  })
  htmltools::div(class = "chart-grid", charts)
}

Distributions

For a histogram in R, pass the result of hist(..., plot = FALSE) to hchart(). See the precomputed histogram example.

A box plot reads five fields per group, low, q1, median, q3 and high.

Show R code 
waits <- data.frame(
  clinic = c("North", "South", "East", "West", "Central", "Coast"),
  lower = c(4, 6, 3, 5, 7, 2),
  p25 = c(6, 8, 5, 8, 10, 5),
  p50 = c(10, 12, 9, 13, 15, 8),
  p75 = c(14, 15, 13, 17, 21, 12),
  upper = c(19, 22, 18, 24, 29, 17)
)
hchart(
  waits,
  "boxplot",
  hcaes(x = clinic, low = lower, q1 = p25, median = p50, q3 = p75, high = upper)
)

The bellcurve series fits a normal curve using the sample mean and standard deviation. This example uses all 32 fuel-economy observations in mtcars. For a kernel density estimate, see Densities.

Show R code 
fuel <- mtcars |> transmute(x = row_number(), y = mpg)
hchart(fuel, "scatter", id = "fuel", visible = FALSE, showInLegend = FALSE) |>
  hc_add_series(
    type = "bellcurve",
    baseSeries = "fuel",
    name = "Normal curve"
  ) |>
  hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "Fuel economy (mpg)"))

Comparing a measurement with a target

The bullet compares ten daily means (y) with a target of 18 °C.

Show R code 
daily <- tibble::tibble(
  name = paste(rep(c("W1", "W2"), each = 5), rep(temperatures$name, 2)),
  y = c(temperatures$y, 18, 19, 17, 20, 18)
)
hchart(
  daily,
  "bullet",
  hcaes(x = name, y = y, target = 18),
  colorByPoint = TRUE
) |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Temperature (°C)")) |>
  hc_size(height = 300)
